thought.text: The version I extracted was the internal build number, not the product version. I'll fix the marker directory to the actual product version (2026.2.1.8):

reasoning_content:
build.txt says "AI-262.9437.185.2621.16467767" — the version is 2026.2.1.8 (per the download path), not 262.9437.185 (that's the internal build number). My regex picked up "262.9437.185.2621" from the AI- build ID, which is wrong. flutter's matcher: `^\.?(AndroidStudio[^\d]*)([\d.]+)` — the directory name must be `.AndroidStudio<something>` followed by a number. The number should be the product version (2026.2.1.8).

Fix: delete the incorrect directory and create `/root/.cache/Google/AndroidStudio2026.2.1.8/system/.home` (major=2026 >= 4.1 → system/.home).

Wait — about the version: the matcher `[\d.]+` against "AndroidStudio2026.2.1.8" → version "2026.2.1.8". Good.

Also, jbr's java is working (JDK 25) → validation passes.

Furthermore, should I also add a PATH entry for /opt/android-studio/bin so that the `studio64` command exists? flutter doesn't call it, but having the binary available is nice. Adding to PATH in .bashrc.

action.command: rm -rf "/root/.cache/Google/AndroidStudio262.9437.185.2621" && mkdir -p /root/.cache/Google/AndroidStudio2026.2.1.8/system && echo "/opt/android-studio" > /root/.cache/Google/AndroidStudio2026.2.1.8/system/.home && echo 'export PATH=$PATH:/opt/android-studio/bin' >> /root/.bashrc && ls /root/.cache/Google/ && cat /root/.cache/Google/AndroidStudio2026.2.1.8/system/.home
